draft.title: Openings and endings
card: An opening hooks the reader. It also sets up the voice (how the narrator sounds) and tells the reader what kind of piece to expect.
the ending settles the main problem or question, so the reader feels the story is complete.
the ending returns to an image, line or setting from the opening. It now means something new because of what has happened.
the ending leaves something open on purpose, so the reader keeps thinking after the last line.
draft.remember: Plan both ends: the opening pulls the reader in, and the ending is chosen to leave a particular effect.

a.q: A story opens with Dara counting the cracked tiles in a hospital corridor. It ends with her counting the same tiles, but now she is smiling. Which ending is this?
a.why: The ending returns to an image from the opening, the tiles, and the change in Dara gives it new meaning. It is not a resolution, because the example does not say that a problem has been settled.
a.clue: What does the ending repeat from the start?

b.q: Leo ends his story with Mina standing at a train platform, holding two tickets. The story never says which train she boards. Leo meant to leave the reader wondering. What is his ending?
opts: A circling back to the opening
An opening that sets up voice
b.why: Leo leaves the choice unanswered on purpose, so the reader keeps thinking. It is not a resolution, because the main question is left open. Nothing here returns to the opening, so it does not circle back.
b.clue: Does the reader find out which train she boards?
